description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts broken down by enrollment level, sex, and race/ethnicity for undergraduate and graduate students. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS institution ID (UNITID) and enrollment level (EFFYLEV).

12-month instructional activity measured in total credit hours and/or contact hours, with undergraduate and graduate activity distinguished by instructional-activity level (UNITID and EFIALV). This table is reported only in odd-numbered years, so 2018 (even) has no data.

Institution-level academic library data for fiscal year 2017-18, including library characteristics, collections, expenditures, and services. The survey applies only to degree-granting institutions; expenditure data are available only for institutions with total expenditures over $100,000.

Institution-level data for the undergraduate selection process for entering first-time, degree/certificate-seeking students, collected for academic year Fall 2018. Each record is identified by institution (UNITID) and includes admission consideration factors, applicants, admitted applicants, admitted students who enrolled, and SAT/ACT scores when the institution requires those tests for admission. The table applies only to institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time students; writing scores are not collected, and admission-consideration responses include “considered but not required” but not “do not know.”

Awards and degrees conferred by 6-digit CIP program, first or second major, award level, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL, with counts for total awards and demographic/gender categories.

Students receiving any degree or certificate, broken down by race/ethnicity and gender. Each institution has one record, uniquely identified by UNITID; the table counts students rather than total awards.

Students receiving awards, broken down by award level, race/ethnicity, gender, and age group. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and AWLEVEL; age categories are under 18, 18–24, 25–39, and 40 or older, but race, gender, and age cannot be cross-tabulated together.

Programs offered and programs offered via distance education, by CIPCODE and award level/status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and CIPCODE; 6-digit CIPCODE records identify award levels offered and offered via distance learning, 2-digit CIPCODE records summarize the number of 6-digit programs in the group, and CIPCODE 99 provides institution totals.
Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, attendance status, and student level (EFLEVEL).

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and student level, with all nine race/ethnicity categories. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, attendance status, and student level (EFALEVEL).

Fall enrollment counts broken down by distance-education status and student level, including exclusive, some, and no distance education; exclusive distance education is further classified by student location relative to the institution. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and student level (EFDELEV).

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, age category (EFBAGE), and student level (LSTUDY). Age-based enrollment is optional in even-numbered years, so 2018 (even) has data where institutions reported it.

First-time freshman counts broken down by state of residence, including counts who graduated high school in the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and state of residence (EFCSTATE). Residence-based enrollment is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2018 (even) is not an optional reporting year and has data collection for this table.

Fall enrollment counts for selected major fields—Education, Engineering, Biological/Life Sciences, Mathematics, Physical Sciences, Business, Law, Dentistry, and Medicine—broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and student level. This table is restricted to four-year institutions, and each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, major field, attendance status, and student level (EFCIPLEV).

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio, restricted to institutions with undergraduate students. Entering-class data are reported only by academic-year institutions; institutions with less-than-one-year programs do not have retention data. This table contains institution-level measures rather than a category-defined multi-record enrollment breakdown.

Institution-level finance data for public institutions using GASB 34/35, including revenues by source, expenditures by functional and natural classifications, endowments, assets, and liabilities. The record grain is one public GASB institution, and detailed functional expenditures and natural classifications for fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest are unavailable from fiscal year 2016 onward.

Institution-level finance data for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB, including revenues by source, expenditures by functional and natural classifications, endowments, assets, and liabilities. The record grain is one FASB institution; detailed functional expenditures and natural classifications for fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest are unavailable from fiscal year 2016 onward.

Institution-level finance data for private for-profit institutions using FASB, including revenues by source, expenditures by functional and natural classifications, and assets and liabilities; endowments are not included. The record grain is one private for-profit FASB institution, and detailed functional expenditures and natural classifications for fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest are unavailable from fiscal year 2016 onward.

Graduation outcomes at 200% of normal time for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, covering bachelor’s degree-seeking cohorts at four-year institutions and any-degree/certificate cohorts at less-than-4-year institutions. The institution and cohort/status define the row grain; outcomes include completion at 100%, 150%, and 200% of normal time. This component is reported only in even-numbered years, so 2018 (even) has data; reporting is required for four-year institutions and optional for less-than-4-year institutions.

Graduation and transfer outcomes at 150% of normal time, broken down by institution type, cohort/status, gender, and race/ethnicity for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates. Records are uniquely defined by UNITID and GRTYPE; four-year institutions include bachelor’s and other-than-bachelor’s cohorts, while two-year institutions include the corresponding undergraduate cohort. Two-year 100%-of-normal-time completions are not available by gender and race/ethnicity.

Graduation and transfer outcomes at 150% of normal time for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at less-than-2-year institutions, including enrollment and completion at 100% and 150% of normal time. The institution, identified by UNITID, is the relevant row grain; this table does not cover two-year or four-year institutions.

Graduation outcomes at 150% of normal time for three financial-aid subcohorts—Pell Grant recipients; subsidized Stafford Loan recipients who did not receive Pell; and students receiving neither aid—covering four-year, two-year, and less-than-2-year institutions. Records are uniquely defined by UNITID and PSGRTYPE; four-year records distinguish bachelor’s from other-than-bachelor’s cohorts. This component is reported only in even-numbered years, so 2018 (even) has data.

Staff counts by occupational category, full- or part-time status, medical-school status, faculty status, tenure status, and contract length for applicable occupations. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPCAT, which combines occupational category and faculty/tenure status.

Counts of full-time instructional staff at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by faculty/tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender, with contract-length detail for staff not on tenure track. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SISCAT, combining faculty/tenure status and academic rank; race/ethnicity and gender reporting became mandatory annually beginning in 2016, so 2018 (even) has data.

Full-time new hires at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by primary occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender, with instructional new hires additionally classified by faculty/tenure status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SNHCAT, which defines the primary occupation and, for instructional staff, faculty/tenure status; race/ethnicity and gender reporting became mandatory annually beginning in 2016, so 2018 (even) has data.

Full- and part-time staff counts by occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and STAFFCAT, combining occupational category with full- or part-time status; race/ethnicity and gender reporting became mandatory annually beginning in 2016, so 2018 (even) has data.

Counts of full-time instructional staff at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by academic rank, faculty status, tenure status, and contract length. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and FACSTAT, the faculty/tenure-status combination; contract-length categories include multi-year, indefinite, annual, and less-than-annual.

Counts, salary outlays, average salaries, and equated 9-month salary measures for full-time nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by academic rank, gender, and number of months worked. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK; salary data are unavailable for staff working fewer than 9 months.
Counts and salary outlays for full-time nonmedical noninstructional staff by occupational category.

Custom comparison-group membership records keyed by the submitting institution’s comparison-group identifier and each comparison institution’s UNITID, with the comparison institution’s name and state. These are the groups institutions submitted for the 2018 Data Feedback Report.

Institution-level response and applicability records keyed by UNITID and survey component, identifying responses, imputed nonresponses, parent/child or multiple-campus reporting, and revised submissions.

Directory and classification information for each institution, including UNITID, name and address, institutional URLs, active and Title IV status, control, level, highest award, and Carnegie classifications.

Institution-level records keyed by UNITID covering educational offerings and award levels, organizational control and affiliations, admissions, special learning opportunities, and related services and athletic associations.

Full-academic-year student charges and attendance costs by institution (UNITID) and student or program category, including undergraduate, graduate, part-time, and qualifying doctoral-professional charges. This applies to institutions whose programs are primarily measured in credit hours and whose predominant calendar is semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or another academic-year system; it also includes published first-time undergraduate attendance-cost information.

Program-level vocational student charges keyed by institution (UNITID) and program, including the number of programs, largest-program attendance costs, and tuition, fees, and books-and-supplies charges for up to five additional programs. This is for institutions with clock-hour programs or primarily occupational credit-hour programs that report charges for the full program length.
Institution-level mission information keyed by UNITID, containing either the institution’s mission statement or the web address where it is available.

Award and enrollment outcomes for degree- and certificate-seeking undergraduates who entered during July 1, 2010–June 30, 2011, measured four, six, and eight years later as of August 31, 2014, August 31, 2016, and August 31, 2018. The table covers four entering groups—first-time full-time, first-time part-time, non-first-time full-time, and non-first-time part-time—each split into Pell recipients and non-Pell recipients; all eligible entrants are assigned to one of these eight subcohorts. Records are uniquely identified by institution (UNITID) and cohort (OMCHRT), and contain revised cohort size plus counts and percentages completing or remaining enrolled.

Financial aid recipients and aid amounts, broken down by student population (full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates versus all undergraduates) and aid type/source. The record grain is institution × student population × aid category, with recipient counts plus total and average dollars; the first-time cohort includes federal, state/local, institutional, and federal/nonfederal loan categories, while the all-undergraduate group includes total grants, Pell Grants, and federal loans.

Average net price and its supporting financial-aid amounts for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in two groups: grant or scholarship recipients and Title IV federal-aid recipients. The record grain is institution × student group, and public institutions’ groups are restricted to students paying in-district or in-state tuition rates.

Military, servicemember, and veteran benefit recipients and benefit amounts, broken down by benefit type (Post-9/11 GI Bill Benefits versus Department of Defense Tuition Assistance) and student level (undergraduate versus graduate). The record grain is institution × student level × benefit category, with recipient counts and total dollars received.
